[[File:Acer buergerianum (Trident Maple).jpg|thumb|264x264px|Trident Maple in Fort Worth, Texas]]
'''''Acer buergerianum''''' ('''trident maple'''; {{zh|t={{linktext|三角楓}}|s=三角枫|p=sānjiǎofēng}}) is a species of [[maple]] native to eastern [[China]] (from [[Shandong]] west to southeastern [[Gansu]], south to [[Guangdong]], and southwest to [[Sichuan]]), [[Taiwan]] and [[Japan]].<ref name=focd>{{cite web|website=Flora of China (draft)|url=http://hua.huh.harvard.edu/china/mss/volume11/Aceraceae-AGH_coauthoring.htm|title=Aceraceae|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060209210809/http://hua.huh.harvard.edu/china/mss/volume11/Aceraceae-AGH_coauthoring.htm|archive-date=2006-02-09}}</ref><ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 1 January 2018}}</ref> The specific epithet is a [[patronym]] honoring Dutch plant hunter J. Buerger (1804-1858).<ref name="Trees2005">{{cite book |last1=Moore |first1=D. |last2=White |first2=J. |date=2005 |orig-date=1st pub. 2002 |title= The Illustrated Encyclopedia of Trees |edition=2nd |location= Portland, Oregon |publisher=Timber press |chapter=Maples |page=627 |isbn=0-88192-751-1}}</ref>

==Description==
It is a small to medium-sized [[deciduous]] [[tree]] reaching a height of 5–20 m with a trunk up to 50 cm diameter. The [[leaf|leaves]] are in opposite pairs, 2.5–8 cm long (excluding the 2–5 cm petiole) and 3.5–6.5 cm broad, hard, glossy dark green above, paler below, usually with three lobes; on mature trees the lobes forward-pointing and with smooth margins, on young trees with more spreading lobes and serrated margins. The [[flower]]s are produced in spring, yellow-green, in pendulous [[corymb]]s; they are small, with five greenish sepals and five yellow-white petals about 2 mm long, and eight stamens. The [[fruit]] is a [[Samara (fruit)|samara]] with two winged [[seed]]s, each seed 4–7 mm diameter, with a 15 mm wing; the wings are forward-pointing and often overlapping each other.<ref name=focd/><ref name="gelderen">{{cite book|author1=C.J. van Gelderen|author2=D.M. van Gelderen|date=1999|title=Maples for Gardens: A Color Encyclopedia}}</ref><ref name=rushforth>{{cite book|last=Rushforth|first=K.|date=1999|title=Trees of Britain and Europe|publisher=Collins|isbn=0-00-220013-9}}.</ref>

The species is variable, and a number of [[variety (biology)|varieties]] have been described:<ref name=focd/>
* ''Acer buergerianum'' var. ''buergerianum''. Hubei, Hunan, Jiangsu, Jiangxi, Shandong, Zhejiang.
* ''Acer buergerianum'' var. ''jiujiangense'' <small>Z.X.Yu.</small> Jiangxi.
* ''Acer buergerianum'' var. ''horizontale'' <small>F.P.Metcalf.</small> Southern Zhejiang.
* ''Acer buergerianum'' var. ''formosanum'' <small>(Hayata ex Koidzumi) Sasaki.</small> Taiwan (endemic).
* ''Acer buergerianum'' var. ''kaiscianense'' <small>(Pampanini) W.P.Fang.</small> Gansu, Hubei, Shaanxi.
* ''Acer buergerianum'' var. ''yentangense'' <small>W.P.Fang & M.Y.Fang.</small> Zhejiang.

A few trees have consistently unlobed leaves; these were first described as a variety ''A. trifidum'' var. ''integrifolium'' Makino (''A. trifidum'' is an old synonym of ''A. buergerianum''), but are now not distinguished from the species.<ref name=makino>Makino Herbarium, Tokyo: {{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20070508171043/http://taxa.soken.ac.jp/makinodb/makino/prep_e/MAK151133.html|title=''Acer trifidum''}}</ref> Occasional unlobed leaves also occur on most trees with otherwise normal three-lobed leaves.<ref name=afm>Mitchell, A. F. (1974). ''A Field Guide to the Trees of Britain and Northern Europe''. Collins {{ISBN|0-00-212035-6}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
It is widely grown in temperate regions as an [[ornamental tree]]. It was introduced very early to [[Japan]], where its name translates as "China maple".<ref name=rushforth/><ref name=kanon>Kanon tree book: [http://kanon101.cool.ne.jp/foto_sinrin/K_kaede/to_kaede/to_kaede.htm ''Acer buergerianum''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090630084034/http://kanon101.cool.ne.jp/foto_sinrin/K_kaede/to_kaede/to_kaede.htm |date=2009-06-30 }} (in Japanese; [https://translate.google.com/translate?hl=en&sl=ja&u=http://kanon101.cool.ne.jp/foto_sinrin/K_kaede/to_kaede/to_kaede.htm&sa=X&oi=translate& google translation])</ref> More recently, it was introduced to [[Europe]] and [[North America]] in 1896, and is now occasionally grown in parks and large gardens there.<ref name=afm/> Mature examples may be seen at [[Westonbirt Arboretum]] in [[England]], the [[Esveld Aceretum]] in [[Boskoop|Boskoop, Netherlands]], [[Arnold Arboretum]] in [[Boston, Massachusetts]] and many other locations.<ref name="gelderen"/>

===Bonsai===
[[Image:BonsaiTridentMaple.jpg|thumb|Trident maple bonsai]]
Trident maple is a popular choice for the art of [[bonsai]] and responds well to techniques that create leaf reduction and [[ramification (botany)|ramification]].<ref name="gelderen"/> It is suitable for many style and sizes of bonsai.<ref name="Ma-Ke_Acer buergerianum ">{{cite web | first=Mark | last=D'Cruz | title=Ma-Ke Bonsai Care Guide for Acer buergerianum | publisher=Ma-Ke Bonsai | url=http://makebonsai.com/guide/bonsailink.asp?quicklink=5030&name=Acer_buergerianum | accessdate=2011-07-05 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110714022834/http://www.makebonsai.com/guide/bonsailink.asp?quicklink=5030&name=Acer_buergerianum | archive-date=2011-07-14 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Cultivars===
Several interesting [[cultivar]]s have been developed, many of these bear Japanese names. Notable cultivars include 'Goshiki Kaede' (striking pink and green [[variegation]]), 'Kifu Nishiki' (roundish, almost un-lobed leaves), 'Mino Yatsubusa' (dwarf with long, narrow leaves) 'Mitsubato Kaede' (distinctive [[Cork (material)|cork]]-like trunk) and 'Naruto' (strongly incurved leaf surface).<ref name="gelderen"/>
